summary: A seven-story, 266,000 sq ft building consolidating roughly 1,500 UCSF global health faculty, staff and students plus the Office of the Chancellor, opened for occupancy September 2014 with a ribbon-cutting that October.

milestones.text: Ribbon-cutting celebrates the opening of Mission Hall

costs.what: Design-build contract amount for Mission Hall, as stated on design-builder Rudolph and Sletten's own project page (the developer/contractor's own marketing material, not an independent source) -- likely covers combined design and construction, not broken out separately

facts.value: This project's geometry is tagged 500 16th St from OpenStreetMap's own addr:housenumber, but UCSF's own press release and the architect's project page both give 550 16th St -- discrepancy flagged, not resolved
WRNS Studio; design-builder Rudolph and Sletten; landscape Andrea Cochran Landscape Architecture
Global health faculty/staff/student space and the Office of the Chancellor

open_questions: Street address is inconsistent: this project's geometry file carries OSM's own 500 16th St tag, but every independent source found (UCSF's press release, the architect's page) says 550 16th St. Not resolved; both this file and its geometry file flag it rather than silently picking one.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, blocked to automated fetches with a 403); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further in this pass; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history.
